name: North Macedonia
summary: North Macedonia taxes residents on worldwide income at a flat 10%. Capital gains are taxed on 90% of the gain (9% effective), but gains on securities and investment fund shares held more than two years are taxed at 0%, and real estate held more than five years is exempt. Dividends are taxed at 10%. There is no net wealth tax, and heirs and donees of the first order of succession are exempt from inheritance and gift tax. No special regime for wealthy arrivals.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Ordinary residence; worldwide income taxed at flat 10% (since 1 January 2023).
regimes.eligibility: Resident with permanent or temporary residence in North Macedonia, the latter meaning 183 days or more within any 12-month period. Non-citizens need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains are taxed at the flat 10% rate on 90% of the realised gain. Gains on securities and investment fund shares held for more than two years are taxed at 0% (since 1 January 2023). Real estate sold more than five years after purchase is exempt (three years if lived in for at least one year).

sources.title: North Macedonia – Individual – Taxes on personal income

open_questions: Whether interests in a limited liability company count as 'securities/shares of capital' for the 2-year 0% rule (the 90% base explicitly covers 'shares of capital') was not confirmed.
Whether the 5-year real estate exemption applies to foreign real estate was not confirmed.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Exempt: IPO securities, inherited/gifted securities sold after two years, long-term state/municipal bonds, inherited/gifted real estate after 5 years (3 if lived in).
capital_gains.rate_basis: Listed securities (domestic and foreign) held >2 years: 0%. Private company share (udel/LLC interest, not a security): 10% x 90% = 9%. Local real estate held >5 years: exempt. Foreign real estate left null: application of the holding-period exemption to foreign property not confirmed.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: Securities and fund shares: 0% after more than 2 years. Real estate: exempt after 5 years, or 3 years if lived in for at least one year before sale.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents taxed on worldwide income with treaty relief (49 treaties).

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed at a flat 10% on the gross amount, withheld by a domestic payer. Residents are taxed on worldwide income, so foreign dividends are taxed at 10% with relief for foreign tax.

sources.title: North Macedonia – Individual – Taxes on personal income

open_questions: Mechanism for crediting foreign WHT on foreign dividends was not verified from statute.
dividends.rate_basis: Flat 10% on gross dividends per PwC Income determination (reviewed 23 Jul 2026).
dividends.withholding_outbound: 10% WHT on dividends paid abroad, reducible under treaty (0%–15%) with prior approval of the tax authority.
dividends.treaty_network: 49 treaties (PwC). No treaty with the United States in the PwC list was confirmed.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax. Municipal property tax applies to real estate (rates not verified in this pass).
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal property tax on real estate under the Law on Property Taxes; rates not verified.

inheritance.summary: Inheritance and gift tax is levied by municipalities under the Law on Property Taxes. The heir or donee in the first order of succession (children, spouse) is exempt. Second order pays 2–3%, third order or unrelated 4–5%.
open_questions: PwC does not name children explicitly; under Macedonian succession law the first order comprises descendants and the spouse (not re-verified).
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Cash, securities and movables are taxed only above the prior year's average annual salary (relevant only to non-exempt heirs).
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts follow the same rules; first-order donees are exempt.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if permanent or temporary residence in North Macedonia; temporary residence means 183 days or more in any 12-month period. Treaty rules prevail.

routes.name: Residence permit
routes.requirements: Not in the EU; all foreigners need a residence permit. Routes not researched in this pass.

corporate.summary: CIT 10% on accounting profit adjusted for non-deductibles. Dividends from domestic taxpayers are exempt. 10% WHT on outbound dividends.
corporate.special_zones: Technological Industrial Development Zones offer incentives (not researched).

sources.title: North Macedonia – Corporate – Taxes on corporate income

us_citizen_notes: No US treaty confirmed; US citizens rely on the US foreign tax credit.

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median asking rent (EUR 2,400/month, about MKD 148,000) of 49 houses for rent of at least 200 m² in Skopje's Centar and Karpoš municipalities (which include Vodno, Crniče, Kozle, Zhdanec and the Bardovci villa area; range EUR 1,000–11,200), from the detail pages of the 122 Centar/Karpoš listings among the first six pages (300 listings) of Pazar3.mk's Skopje houses/villas-for-rent search on 2026-10-15. Listings with a placeholder price (EUR 1) and two explicitly for business use were excluded. Rooms are given as total rooms, so floor area is the size filter. Asking prices on a listing portal.

source.title: Куќи/Вили – Издавање – Скопје (houses/villas for rent, Skopje)

intl_school_annual_fee.description: NOVA International School Skopje (IB World School, PreK–12), 2026–27 'regular tuition' for international citizens, Grades 11–12 (IB Diploma years): EUR 15,600 a year. Citizens of North Macedonia pay a reduced EUR 8,300. Extra: EUR 450 enrolment fee and EUR 500–3,000 capital fee a year (EUR 3,000 for families on regular tuition), EUR 1,000 tuition deposit and EUR 150 application fee for new students, IB DP exams about EUR 102 per exam. The school notes the higher Early Education rate applies when an employer pays; for Grades 11–12 the international rate is the only one shown for foreigners.

cost_of_living.notes: Rent from Pazar3.mk listing detail pages (Centar and Karpoš); school fee from NOVA's own 2026–27 fee page. QSI International School of Skopje does not publish tuition (only a USD 600 registration fee).
